findings.description: NRM-49 asserts `[ "$took" -lt 15 ]` on the real wall clock (`$SECONDS`) around a process_findings call that runs four ~120 KB payloads, two of which are rejected and go through the repair chain (lock acquisition, status files, sidecar writes). The suite's own rule, stated in NRM-26 and NRM-27 ("the test's own clock — no wall-clock margin to flake under load", run 23 c2b DISS-C-001), moved every timing expectation onto `_fake_repair_clock`; this test re-introduces a wall-clock bound. The round-20 dry run already saw NRM-22/NRM-26 race a whole-second budget guard under load, which is the same failure shape.
findings.failure_mode: On a loaded CI runner (parallel bats files, the dissent driver's other suites, a slow jq build) the four-payload run crosses 15 s and the test fails with no defect in the code under test; conversely the bound is loose enough that a quadratic regression on a single 120 KB payload (the 54 s case was 300 KB) can still pass well under 15 s, so the guard is both flaky and weak.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the wall-clock assertion with a structural one: pin that the rewritten predicates are linear by running the same payload at two sizes (e.g. 40k and 80k runs) under `_fake_repair_clock`-independent measurement of jq work, or assert the absence of the whole-string `gsub` directly in the extracted jq programs (grep the derive/clean filters for `gsub(` over the full string). If a timing bound is kept, use a per-size ratio (time(2n)/time(n) < 3) rather than an absolute 15 s, and document the slack rule the other tests follow.

findings.description: The operand lint in NRM-46 is an allowlist that must fail on every unreviewed way a payload-sized value reaches jq. Its environment rule is `(?:^|[\s;&|(])[A-Za-z_]\w*=\S*\s+(?:command\s+)?jq\b`. The `\S*` for the assigned value cannot span whitespace, so an env prefix whose quoted value contains a space — `P="x $finding_json" jq '$ENV.P'`, `P="${a} ${payload}" jq …`, or `P="$(printf '%s %s' …)" jq …` — never matches, and the `$ENV`/`env.` branch only fires when the jq program is on the same line (a program held in a variable, `jq -n "$prog"`, hides `$ENV.P`). The fixture set exercises only the single-token `P="$finding_json" jq` shape, so the gap is not covered by the lint's own positive/negative controls.
findings.failure_mode: A future edit that passes a payload through jq's environment with any whitespace in the value (or with the program in a variable) passes the lint silently; at runtime the envp string exceeds MAX_ARG_STRLEN and jq fails with E2BIG exactly like the argv case the lint exists to prevent (the exit-126 envelope loss from run 29).
findings.suggested_fix: In the environment rule, match the value as a shell word rather than `\S*`: allow quoted spans, e.g. `[A-Za-z_]\w*=(?:"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|'[^']*'|\S)*\s+(?:command\s+)?jq\b`, and flag any such prefix whose value interpolates a name outside SMALL (reuse the existing `re.findall(r'\$\{?([A-Za-z_0-9]+)', …)` check). Add two fixtures to the NRM-46 control set: `P="x $finding_json" jq -n '$ENV.P'` must be caught, and `P="$model $i" jq -n '$ENV.P'` must pass.
